proposals.before: During Wei's Zhenguang era, Mohe Chen Bajie overran the frontier garrisons, and Wang Meng was swept up with his forces.
proposals.after: During Wei's Zhenguang era, Poliuhan Baling overran the frontier garrisons, and Wang Meng was swept up with his forces.
proposals.reason: 破六汗拔陵 is the rebel Poliuhan/Poliuohan Baling, not the unrelated English name Mohe Chen Bajie.

proposals.before: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, Mohe Chen Bajie attacked and captured the garrison towns, and Meng too was swept up in his host.
proposals.after: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, Poliuhan Baling attacked and captured the garrison towns, and Meng too was swept up in his host.
proposals.reason: The literal English repeats the same false rendering of 破六汗拔陵.

proposals.before: As vanguard under He Ba Yue he helped capture Moqi Chounu and pacify Qin and Long, often first over the wall and fighting at the fore.
proposals.after: As vanguard under Heba Yue he helped capture Moqi Chounu and pacify Qin and Long, often first over the wall and fighting at the fore.
proposals.reason: 賀拔岳 is the compound surname Heba plus given name Yue, not He plus Ba Yue.

proposals.before: He escorted Empress Ai, consort of Emperor Wen of Wei, back from the Rouran.
proposals.after: He escorted Empress Dao, consort of Emperor Wen of Wei, back from the Rouran.
proposals.reason: 悼后 is Empress Dao (posthumous 悼), not Empress Ai (哀).

proposals.before: He welcomed Empress Ai, consort of Emperor Wen of Wei, from the Rouran.
proposals.after: He welcomed Empress Dao, consort of Emperor Wen of Wei, from the Rouran.
proposals.reason: The literal line likewise mistranslates 悼 as Ai.

proposals.before: Following He Ba Yue as vanguard, he captured Moqi Chounu, pacified Qin and Long, and was often first to scale the walls and fight hard.
proposals.after: Following Heba Yue as vanguard, he captured Moqi Chounu, pacified Qin and Long, and was often first to scale the walls and fight hard.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise splits the surname 賀拔 into He Ba.

proposals.before: In the Deposed Emperor's second year he became governor of South Qishan, was raised to Duke of Anning, and his fief reached two thousand households in all.
proposals.after: In the Deposed Emperor's second year he became governor of Nanqi, was raised to Duke of Anning, and his fief reached two thousand households in all.
proposals.reason: Nanqi Province is 南岐州, not South Qishan; Qi here is the provincial name, not Mount Qi.

proposals.before: Even on campaign he gathered Confucian scholars and had them taught the classics and histories.
proposals.after: Even on campaign, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai broadly gathered Confucian scholars and had Xiang taught the classics and histories.
proposals.reason: After Tai cherished Xiang, the next sentence continues Tai as the agent who gathered scholars to teach Xiang the classics.

proposals.before: At seventeen he left office and became supernumerary attendant at court, given the added rank general of awesome might.
proposals.after: At seventeen he doffed plain clothes and became supernumerary attendant at court, given the added rank general of awesome might.
proposals.reason: 解褓 means first entering official service, not leaving office.

proposals.before: While Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power, he and He Lanxiang—cousins by marriage and friends from youth—planned military and state affairs together.
proposals.after: While Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu held power, he and He Lanxiang—cross-cousins (zhongbiao) and friends from youth—planned military and state affairs together.
proposals.reason: 中表 denotes cross-cousins (children of a father's sister or mother's siblings), not cousins by marriage.

proposals.before: Our late emperor, divinely martial, answered the age; he set the realm right in one stroke; east he conquered, south he cut down, and none who thought of resisting submitted.
proposals.after: Our late emperor, divinely martial, answered the age; he set the realm right in one stroke; east he conquered, south he cut down, and none who thought of resisting went unsubdued.
proposals.reason: 無思不服 means none who contemplated resistance remained unsubmissive; the current literal reverses the double negative into 'submitted' after 'resisting'.

proposals.before: If you can turn calamity into blessing, deeply recognize what the times require, and ruler and ministers together come bearing coffins and kowtow in submission, then ranks and titles will be removed and you will forever guard the western domains;
proposals.after: If you can turn calamity into blessing, deeply recognize what the times require, and ruler and ministers together come bearing coffins and kowtow in submission, then ranks and titles will be clearly conferred and you will forever guard the western domains;
proposals.reason: 爵等顯除 means ranks will be plainly granted/appointed, not that titles will be stripped.

proposals.before: Hong and Er counties and made the territory Taozhou.
proposals.after: Honghe, two cities, and made the territory Taozhou.
proposals.reason: 洪和二城 names the two cities of Honghe together with Taoyang in s0152, not separate counties Hong and Er.

proposals.before: Hong and Er counties, and made the territory Taozhou.
proposals.after: Honghe, two cities, and made the territory Taozhou.
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic line: 洪和 is one toponym plus 二城, not Hong and Er counties.

proposals.before: [In Jiande fifth year Can followed Emperor Wen at Bing Province, fell in battle, and was posthumously made upper grand general and Duke of Qingdu.
proposals.after: [In Jiande fifth year Can followed Gaozu at Bing Province, fell in battle, and was posthumously made upper grand general and Duke of Qingdu.
proposals.reason: 高祖 in the Zhou shu is temple-name Gaozu (Northern Zhou Emperor Wu), not Emperor Wen.

proposals.before: [In Jiande fifth year, following Emperor Wen at Bing Province, he died in battle, posthumously awarded upper grand general, and posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Qingdu commandery.
proposals.after: [In Jiande fifth year, following Gaozu at Bing Province, he died in battle, posthumously awarded upper grand general, and posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Qingdu commandery.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 高祖 as Emperor Wen, which is the wrong sovereign.

proposals.before: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said delightedly: "When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine mouth."
proposals.after: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said delightedly: "When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine servant."
proposals.reason: 佳口 is a prized dependent counted as a 'mouth', not a literal mouth; s0194 then grants two maids.

proposals.before: The Grand Progenitor said in delight: "When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine mouth."
proposals.after: The Grand Progenitor said in delight: "When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine servant."
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 佳口 as a body part rather than a servant.

proposals.before: Because Empress Ashina was about to enter from the Turks, Chen Gongchun and others had an edict issued summoning Chigang and Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the frontier.
proposals.after: Because Empress Ashina was about to enter the frontier from the Turks, an edict summoned Gang and Grand General Wang Jie, in connection with Duke of Chen Chun and others, to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the border.
proposals.reason: 陳公純 is Duke of Chen, given name Chun, not the fused 'Chen Gongchun'; 詔徵 is an imperial edict summoning Gang and Wang Jie, not an edict issued by Chun.

proposals.before: Chen Gongchun and others, because Empress Ashina was about to enter the frontier from the Turks, an edict summoned Gang together with Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the border.
proposals.after: Duke of Chen, Chun, and others, because Empress Ashina was about to enter the frontier from the Turks, an edict summoned Gang together with Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the border.
proposals.reason: 陳公純 is a title plus given name (Duke of Chen, Chun), not the unhistorical compound Chen Gongchun.

proposals.before: Soon he was removed and made governor of Shanwu commandery.
proposals.after: Soon he was appointed governor of Shanwu commandery.
proposals.reason: 除 here is appointment to office, not removal.

proposals.before: In the third year of Xiaochang, he was again removed and made separate commander, following Changsun Zhi on the western campaign.
proposals.after: In the third year of Xiaochang, he was again appointed separate commander, following Changsun Zhi on the western campaign.
proposals.reason: 又除 is a further appointment; 除 does not mean 'removed'.

proposals.before: He also gave him a daughter of Duke Hui of Shao Yuwen Hao in marriage.
proposals.after: He also gave him a daughter of Duke Hui of Shao in marriage.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names only 邵惠公; 'Yuwen Hao' is an interpolated identification not in the source sentence.

proposals.before: At the start of Tianhe, he was removed and made left palace guard, and advanced in rank to grand general.
proposals.after: At the start of Tianhe, he was appointed left palace guard, and advanced in rank to grand general.
proposals.reason: 除左宮伯 is appointment, not removal from office.

proposals.before: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, he was sent out as governor of He Province, raised to Duke of Shibao, and given a thousand more households.
proposals.after: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, he was sent out as governor of He Province, raised to Duke of Shibao, and given a thousand more households.
proposals.reason: 孝閔帝 is Emperor Xiaomin of Northern Zhou; 'Xiaojing' is not in the source and is a mistranslation of the posthumous title.

proposals.before: When Emperor Min of Xiaojing succeeded, he went out as governor of He Province, advanced in nobility to Duke of Shibao county, and given an increased fief of one thousand households.
proposals.after: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, he went out as governor of He Province, advanced in nobility to Duke of Shibao county, and was given an increased fief of one thousand households.
proposals.reason: 孝閔帝 is Emperor Xiaomin, not 'Emperor Min of Xiaojing'; the English also lacks a finite verb ('and given').

proposals.before: He entered court as junior minister of works, was removed and made governor of Yun Province, and transferred to governor of Ning Province.
proposals.after: He entered court as junior minister of works, was appointed governor of Yun Province, and transferred to governor of Ning Province.
proposals.reason: 除 here means to appoint to office, not to remove from office.

decisions.reason: s0006 names 破六汗拔陵, the Six Garrisons rebel Poliuhan Baling; Mohe Chen Bajie is an unrelated misreading of that name.
The literal of s0006 likewise must render 破六汗拔陵 as Poliuhan Baling, not Mohe Chen Bajie.
s0011 has 賀拔岳, the compound surname 賀拔 plus given name 岳; splitting it as He Ba Yue is a naming error.
s0018 has 悼后; 悼 is the posthumous Dao, not 哀 (Ai).
The literal of s0018 likewise mistranslates 悼后 as Empress Ai; Empress Dao matches 悼.
Literal s0011 repeats the split of 賀拔岳; Heba Yue restores the compound surname.
s0052 has 南岐州刺史: Nanqi is the province name, not South Qishan (岐山).

decisions.after: Even on campaign he gathered Confucian scholars to instruct him in the classics and histories.
decisions.reason: s0076 教以書傳 means instruction in the classics, so the original 'had them taught' inverts patient and teacher; the unit does not name Tai as the gatherer, so inserting Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai over-reads 特為太祖所愛 in s0075.
s0078 解褐 is doffing plain clothes to take first office, not leaving office.
s0119 中表 is cross-cousin kinship, not cousins by marriage.
s0125 無思不服 is a double negative: none who thought of resistance remained unsubmissive; 'none who thought of resisting submitted' reverses that sense.
In s0148 爵等顯除, 除 is appointment and 顯 is 'plainly'; after 輿櫬稽顙 the offer is to confer ranks, not strip them.
With s0152 洮陽, s0154 洪和二城 are the two cities Taoyang and Honghe, not counties Hong and Er.
Literal s0154 repeats the split of 洪和二城; Honghe plus 'two cities' restores the toponym.
s0167 高祖 in this Zhou shu note is temple-name Gaozu (Jiande 5), not Emperor Wen.
The literal of s0167 likewise must render 高祖 as Gaozu, not Emperor Wen.
s0193 佳口 is a prized dependent; s0194 賜綱侍婢二人 shows the reward was servants, not a body part.
Literal s0193 repeats the body-part reading of 佳口; 'fine servant' matches the sense confirmed in s0194.

decisions.after: When Duke of Chen Chun and others were bringing Empress Ashina from the Turks to enter the frontier, an edict summoned Chigang and Grand General Wang Jie to lead troops to welcome and escort her at the frontier.
decisions.reason: s0210 陳公純 is Duke of Chen, Chun, not Chen Gongchun, and 詔徵綱與大將軍王傑 is an imperial summons of Gang and Wang Jie, not an edict issued by Chun; the proposed 'in connection with' is awkward and blurs that 陳公純等 belongs with the incoming of 皇后阿史那氏.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 陳公純等以皇后阿史那氏自突厥將入塞，詔徵綱與大將軍王傑

decisions.reason: Literal s0210 already treats 詔徵 as an edict summoning Gang and Wang Jie; replacing Chen Gongchun with Duke of Chen, Chun matches 陳公純.
s0229 尋除善無郡守 uses 除 as appointment to office, not removal.
s0230 又除別將 is a further appointment; 除 does not mean he was removed.
s0235 names only 邵惠公女; Yuwen Hao is not in this sentence and should not be interpolated.
s0247 除左宮伯 is appointment as left palace guard, not removal from office.
s0270 孝閔帝 is Emperor Xiaomin; 'Emperor Min of Xiaojing' splits the title and invents Jing.
Literal s0270 likewise needs Emperor Xiaomin for 孝閔帝, and 'was given' supplies the missing finite verb.
s0274 除雲州刺史 uses 除 as appointment, not removal from the junior ministership.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0015 shows Emperor Wen was created solely by mistranslating 高祖; the temple-name Gaozu is already claimed as c0308, and this unit does not support an Emperor Wen title.
Revised r0019 shows Chen Gongchun is a fused non-name; 陳公 and 純 remain as title and given-name claims, and no personal name Chen Gongchun is in the source.
Accepted r0023 removes interpolated Yuwen Hao; s0235 only supports the title 邵惠公 already claimed as c0469, not the personal name Yuwen Hao.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Mohe Chen Bajie came only from misreading 破六汗拔陵; the personal-name claim must use Poliuhan Baling.
Accepted r0003 restores the compound surname 賀拔; the English personal name must be Heba Yue, matching the existing pinyin.
Accepted r0004 shows Empress Ai was produced by reading 悼 as 哀; the title claim must be Empress Dao.

value.text: When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine mouth.
When the matter is settled, I shall reward you with a fine servant.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0017 restores 佳口 as a servant; the quoted speech on the attribution claim must match the repaired English.
Accepted r0025 shows Emperor Min of Xiaojing came only from splitting 孝閔帝; the title claim must be Emperor Xiaomin.
